title: Ya sos nica
desc: An ordinary Saturday, and somebody says it out loud
setting: It is eleven thirty on a Saturday at doña Elena's, there are twenty people between the patio and the kitchen, and nothing is being celebrated.

steps.speaker: Doña Elena
steps.es: Póngale sal a esa olla, mijo. Usted ya sabe cuánto.
steps.en: Put salt in that pot, son. You know how much by now.

options.feedback: She stopped measuring years ago and so have you. Nobody in that kitchen is going to remark on it, which is the point.
You know. Asking hands the decision back to her when she has just handed it to you.

options.en: Better if you put it in.
options.feedback: She asked because it does not matter any more who does it. Handing the pot back puts you two years into the past.

steps.speaker: Don Beto
steps.es: Ideay, ¿y este a qué hora llegó?
steps.en: Ideay, and what time did this one get here?

options.es: A las once y media, don Beto. La hora buena.
options.en: Half past eleven, don Beto. The right hour.
options.feedback: They said eleven. You came at half past, which is the hour the invitation actually meant, and saying so out loud is the joke he was setting up.
Fine. The half hour is the funny part and you left it out.
You did not, and everybody saw you arrive. Five years ago you would have, and that is the joke.

steps.speaker: Don Beto
steps.es: Miren a este. Ya sos nica, vos.
steps.en: Look at this one. You are a nica now, you are.

options.feedback: Take it and hand a bit of it back. Claiming it whole would be too much and refusing it would be worse, and adoptivo is the word people use.
Warm, and it treats it as a compliment. It is more like a decision the room has made.
He said it in front of twenty people, which is how these things are made official here. Arguing with it argues with all of them.

steps.speaker: Doña Elena
steps.es: ¿Y ese chavalo suyo dónde anda? Que venga a comer.
steps.en: And where is that boy of yours? Tell him to come and eat.

options.es: Ahí anda con los primos. Ya lo llamo, doña.
options.en: He is off with his cousins. I will call him, doña.
options.feedback: Your son is somewhere in a house full of people who are all his family. Nobody has explained anything to you in about two years and you did not need it.
True. Con los primos is the part that says where he actually belongs.
That has never once been an acceptable answer in this kitchen, and you learned it in your first month.
